lessons.title: Daily and weekly care
lessons.html:
Caring for plants in a nursery or garden

Ornamental plants are grown for their looks: flowers, leaves, shape. Whether they are in pots in a nursery or in beds in a garden, they need regular care to stay healthy and attractive. Most of this care is done every day or every week.

Watering

  • Check soil moisture with your finger. Water when the top few centimetres are dry, unless the plant needs different care.
  • Water the soil, not the leaves, to reduce disease.
  • Water deeply and less often for plants in beds. Pots dry out faster and may need daily watering in summer.
  • Water early in the day.
  • Follow municipal water restrictions.

Weeding

Weeds take water, food and light. Pull them by hand while small, including roots. In pots, remove weeds every time you see them. Hoe beds lightly so you do not damage plant roots.

Grooming

  • Remove dead and yellow leaves.
  • Deadhead old flowers.
  • Tie in climbers and stake tall plants.
  • Space pot plants in the nursery so leaves do not touch, for air flow.

Checking for problems

As you work, look for pests, disease, wilting, yellowing and broken stems. Report what you find to your supervisor. Early action saves plants.

lessons.title: Feeding, mulching, pruning and record keeping
lessons.html:
Feeding

Plants in pots use up nutrients in the potting mix, and nutrients wash out with watering. Feed according to the programme your supervisor gives: slow-release granules, liquid feeds or fertiliser on beds. Always measure, apply to moist soil, keep fertiliser off leaves and stems, and water in.

Mulching

Mulch is a layer of material on top of the soil, such as bark chips, compost, straw or pebbles. It:

  • keeps the soil moist and cool
  • stops weeds
  • adds organic matter as it breaks down (organic mulches)
  • makes beds look neat

Spread mulch about 50–75 mm deep and keep it a hand's width away from stems and trunks.

Light pruning and trimming

Trim plants to keep a good shape and remove the three Ds: dead, diseased and damaged parts. Use sharp, clean tools. Larger pruning jobs follow the supervisor's schedule.

Potting on

When a pot plant fills its pot with roots, it is potted on into a bigger pot with fresh mix. Signs: roots coming out of the drainage holes, the plant drying out very fast, or the plant falling over.

Record keeping

Write down what you did on the work sheet or job card: watering, feeding (product and amount), spraying, pests found. Good records help the team plan and prove that work was done.

Safety

  • Wear gloves and wash hands after handling fertiliser, compost and potting mix.
  • Wear a hat and sunscreen and drink water.
  • Lift pots and bags correctly.
  • Keep paths clear of hoses and tools.

Key points

  • Check moisture before watering and water the soil, not the leaves.
  • Remove weeds while small.
  • Feed according to the programme and water fertiliser in.
  • Mulch 50–75 mm deep, away from stems.
  • Report problems early and record all work.
